Commentary.Commentary: It's a stiff target in front of the Kiwis. The highest successful chase at this venue is 201 and they will have to create history to win this series 2-0. Don't think they can approach the final innings with a defensive frame of mind and aiming for a draw as they already lead the series 1-0. The conditions have turned overcast and it will assist the English seamers. Definitely going to be challenging for the home team. Stay tuned for their reply.

Another good batting show by the Englishmen. Almost every batsman contributed and we saw plenty of partnerships. Mark Stoneman, James Vince and Dawid Malan, the supposedly weaker link of England's batting line-up, scored handy fifties while Joe Root and Jonny Bairstow also were brilliant. For New Zealand, it was a real struggle yesterday. They had to work hard for wickets. Trent Boult and Tim Southee failed to have the same impact and Colin de Grandhomme who finished with a 4-fer was the most successful bowler.

So, as expected, England came out after Lunch and made their intentions clear. Their batsmen looked for quick runs and lost wickets in the process as well. But once again Jonny Bairstow played his part, scoring handy runs and the lower order also contributed. It started to drizzle a bit and maybe, that prompted the English skipper to make the declaration, otherwise one would think that the psychological 400 mark would have been in his mind.

OUT! Bairstow is bounced out! Wagner picks up his second wicket. He bangs in a short ball, angling away outside off. Bairstow moves across to play the pull shot but ends up getting a top edge. The ball goes high in the air and Henry Nicholls comes a couple of steps ahead from deep square leg to take a safe catch. That's it from England, they have DECLARED. 382 is the target for New Zealand.
Similar delivery, this time the southpaw gets it off the inner half through square leg. Brings Jonny back on strike.
Angling in on middle, Leach works it away on the leg side.
Fuller in length and outside off, Bairstow drives it through extra cover for a single. Partnership is now 39 from 37 balls.
Neil Wagner is back on.
Good length, angling away from off, Leach shoulders his arms.
Gets forward, reaches to the pitch, drives well but can't find the gap.
FOUR! 350 up for England! Jack Leach joins in the fun now! Stands back to a short ball, Southee offers width and it's slapped through point for a boundary.
Fuller in length and swinging away a bit, Leach has a waft at it. Gets beaten.
Length ball outside off, defended down.

Good stop from Boult! On a back of a length outside off, Leach taps it towards backward point where Trent dives to his left to stop it. He then releases it at the bowler's end but it hits the bat of Bairstow who was dragging it in.
FOUR! Jonny Bairstow is taking the attack to the opposition now. Makes room to a fuller ball served outside off and drills it through cover. Not a soul moved. Lead now touches 375. 16 from the over.
Driven hard but finds the man at cover.
FOUR! England on the charge! Short ball on middle and leg, Jonny pulls it down to fine leg for another boundary, second of the over.
Fuller delivery on the pads, flicked past the umpire at square leg for a couple more.
FOUR! Whacked! Boult bowls it short on middle, Bairstow hangs back and powers it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Nice punch on the up! Boult delivers it full outside off, Jonny punches it past mid off and picks up a double to his name.
There is a bit of drizzle in the air and the groundsmen are getting ready...

Direct hit would have been curtains for Jack Leach! Bairstow works a length ball in front of square leg and scampers across to the other end. This is a misjudged run, never on but the fielder misses his shy at the striker's end. Leach, who had given up all the hope, survives.
Good length ball on middle and off, it's stroked past Williamson at gully for a run.
Another back foot punch by Leach but this time he finds the fielder at cover-point.
Very well played by Leach. Back of a length ball on off, Jack delays his back foot punch a bit and then places it through point for a couple.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Starts by angling a length ball outside off, Leach shoulders arms.
Tim Southee returns. Colin de Grandhomme gets a break after going for 10 runs in his last over. Poor guy is just one away from his maiden Test fifer. Must be feeling bad.
Digs in a short ball on off, Bairstow tries to hook but misses.
Strides forward to a full ball and drives it straight to mid off.
It's gone pretty dark out there. The clouds have built up slowly.
Bouncer this time by Trent, around middle, the keeper-batsman ducks.
On a length and around off, Jonny punches it to covers.
A length ball on middle, Jonny defends it by getting forward.
Hops inside the crease and plays it down with soft hands to point for a run.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point. 10 from the over.
FOUR! Turning out to be a good over for England! Bairstow spots the width outside off and slams it through point for a boundary.
Pitches it full and outside off, it's driven brilliantly through covers for three. Lead now touches 350!
On middle, Bairstow works it in the acres of space at mid-wicket and jogs across for a single.
Colin changes his angle for the left-hander. Bowls it from 'round the wicket and hurls a length ball on middle, Leach nudges it behind to fine leg and takes a run.
Lands it on a length outside off, Bairstow pushes it with an angled bat to point. Runs the first run hard, wants the second but the fielder gets to the ball and stops him in his tracks.
Straighter in line, it's worked towards mid on where Sodhi dives all over it and misfields. Concedes a single.
Identical to the last delivery, this time Leach plays a square drive and collects a single. His partner eyes the second run but it's not on.
Serves it full and outside off, inviting a drive but Jack is content in leaving it.
Good length ball on off, it's punched off the back foot to covers.
Bouncer to Leach by Boult, the debutant ducks.
Taps it down in the gap at covers for a single.
Jack Leach is the new batsman. He did a good job in the first innings by playing a supporting role to Jonny. Can he do it again?

OUT! Straight through the gate! Colin gets his fourth and will be smelling his maiden fifer in Tests. Delivers a full length ball around off, shaping back in a bit, Wood swings across the line without accounting for the movement and misses the ball completely. The stumps are shattered and Wood returns. England's lead is 9 short of 350!
FOUR! Another cracking shot by Wood! He is making his case for batting ahead of Broad. Latches onto a delivery wide outside off and smacks it through covers.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! We saw a few from his bat in the first essay. A short ball angling into the batsman, the pace of Colin won't trouble Wood as he goes back and pulls it powerfully to the deep mid-wicket fence.
Short and on off, a mistimed pull wide of mid on for a run.
Short in length and outside off, Jonny tries to pull but misses.
Runs in from around the wicket and angles in a length ball on off, Wood defends it off his back foot.
Outside off, another play and a miss from Wood.
Goes full outside off, it's driven off the front foot to mid off.
Again it lands outside off, Wood feels for it and gets beaten.
Beaten! Boult bowls it on a length around off, angling away, Wood pokes inside the line and misses.
Slants it away from the batsman, Bairstow steers it through point for a single.
Defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fullish and outside off, it's pushed out to point.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Angling into the batsman, Bairstow knocks it down to mid on for a run.
Full and outside off, Jonny tries to drive but misses as it beats the inside edge.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.

Dropped by Boult but that was travelling. Would have been a stunning return catch. Full and around off, it's driven back firmly. Goes uppishly and Boult sticks his left hand out. Fails to hold on. Another life for Jonny.
Bairstow has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Play and a miss! Boult takes a length ball away from the batsman, outside off, Jonny once again in this over feels for it and gets beaten.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Angling away from the batsman, outside off, Bairstow pushes at it and misses.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
On a length and outside off, Wood pushes at it and edges it behind towards gully. Doesn't carry.
Mark Wood is in next. He joins Bairstow in the middle. This pair did an amazing job in the first innings. England will be hoping for something similar again.

OUT! Colin de Grandhomme gets his revenge after going for 12 runs in this over. The change in pace does the trick. Colin delivers it at 96.6 kph, around middle and on a length, Broad attempts for a big heave across the line but mistimes it in the air. Ish Sodhi, who has got hardly anything to do today, gets a low ball in front of him and he dives forward to take it at mid on. End of a short little cameo by Stuart. New Zealand doing well by picking regular wickets.

FOUR! Booming shot by Broad. He is trying to attack Colin here. Latches onto a full delivery wide outside off and drills it square of the wicket on the off side for a powerful boundary. 300 up for England!
Sliding down the leg side, Bairstow fails to flick and it goes off his pads to square leg. A leg bye taken.
This one cuts back into the batsman from a length around off, Broad turns it through mid-wicket and takes three.
FOUR! Glorious, this time from Broad. He receives a full ball in his half and drives it beautifully through mid off for a boundary.

FOUR! Boult serves it full and wide outside off, Bairstow strides forward and drives it crisply through covers for a glorious boundary. End of the over, Boult will be feeling hard done by as he had Jonny.
A length ball around off, Broad stays back to push inside the line. Gets an outside edge wide of the slip cordon and they cross.
Good length delivery outside off, punched from the back foot to point.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Gets on the front foot and drives it through point for a run.

Edged and gone, noooo! It's not given. Boult delivers a cutter around off, Bairstow gets forward with a straight bat to defend but fails to middle it. There is some sound as it goes past his bat and the keeper jumps in joy after catching the ball. They all appeal but nothing from the umpire. New Zealand have no reviews left. And...the replays detect a big spike. Oh dear, bad luck for the Kiwis.
Good length delivery outside off, Broad allows it through.
Stuart Broad is in next.

OUT! Jeet Raval has taken a ripper as New Zealand get rid of Ben Stokes soon after the Lunch break. Colin de Grandhomme continues from around the wicket and angles in a full ball around off, Stokes gets forward and across to flick it on the leg side but fails to keep it down. Jeet Raval at mid-wicket flies to his left and takes an excellent catch. Stokes is disappointed with himself as he walks to the pavilion. Lead - 311!
Four byes! A length ball around off, nipping away to beat the bat of Stokes. Watling has no chance of cutting it off and it races behind for a boundary. The keeper standing up didn't help either.
Angles in a length ball on middle, Stokes defends it from the crease.
Pitches it up and outside off, it's driven down to mid off.
Starts with a driving length ball outside off, Stokes strokes it through the line, it's a bit uppish but not carrying to the cover fielder. On one bounce it goes.

Back for the afternoon session. The players are making their way back on the field. One can sense a counter-punch here from England and they have two big hitters to do that job. Having said that, the Kiwis will be operating with the second new ball and will be hoping to pick quick wickets. Game on. Colin de Grandhomme to continue. The keeper is standing up and there are two slips in place. Here we go...
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

Soon it got rubbed on his partner as Neil Wagner got rid of Joe Root in the following over to lift the morale his side which seemed to be sinking with every passing over. Post that, Kane Williamson didn't waste any time as he took the second new ball but Ben Stokes and Jonny Bairstow saw it through safely. With Tim Southee unwell, it's a huge responsibility on the rest to stop England from setting a big target. The lead has already crossed the 300-run mark. Can the Kiwis restrict it to a gettable one? Or will the Englishmen continue to stretch it? An action-packed session awaits. Do join us shortly...

The session which was turning out to be a one-way traffic, suddenly spiced up just towards the end. The overnight pair of Joe Root and Dawid Malan were going along well in the first hour as they were scoring at around 4 runs per over. Both looked set, assured and notched their respective fifties. It seemed like they would run away with the show but all of a sudden, out of nowhere, Colin de Grandhomme removed Malan to become the first non-new ball bowler to pick up a wicket in this Test.
Switches the angle for the last ball of the over. Comes from around the wicket and hurls it outside off, it comes back in but Bairstow has it covered as he makes an assured leave. LUNCH ON DAY 4!
Pitches it right up there, Jonny leans ahead as he drives it straight to the cover fielder.
Fullish outside off, Bairstow lifts his bat to leave it alone.
Fuller and swinging back in on middle, worked off the inner half to mid-wicket.
Leg bye! Good length delivery, angling in on the pads, Ben tries to work it away but gets it off the pads towards fine leg. A leg bye taken.
Keeps it nice and full on off, Stokes presses ahead to defend but the ball shapes away a bit. Takes the edge and rolls towards gully. He played it with soft hands that is why the edge didn't carry.
Last over before Lunch, can NZ pick up another wicket?
On a good length and shaping away a touch, no harm for the keeper-batsman as he is happy to push it away. A maiden!
Knows the ball is jagging away so Bairstow covers the swing well as he keeps it out.
Slightly fuller in length, on off, Jonny B prods ahead and defends it down.
Third leave in a row! Touch fuller and hurled outside off, JB is happy to make another leave.
Pitches it up outside off and keeps moving away, Jonny lifts his bat to let it be.
Some swing for Colin! He lands it on a length around off, it curls away, Bairstow lets it pass.
Fuller again from Boult, Stokes lunges forward to defend but gets it off the edge towards point, along the ground.
Presses forward to a fuller delivery and stabs it out firmly.
Fuller and veering on the pads, Stokes whip/flicks it down to fine leg to get a couple.
Makes him play by pitching it up and bowling it on the stumps, Stokes keeps it out.
Another one on a similar length outside off, another leave follows.
In the channel outside off, Ben shoulders his arms.
Comes forward to a fuller delivery and defends it well.
On the pads, not good from Colin. Glanced behind square on the leg side for a single.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

FOUR! Edged but safe! On a length and at a gentle pace outside off, it's the new cherry and that is why it skids a bit off the deck, Stokes pokes at it and gets a thick edge which flies past the diving first slip fielder for a boundary. A streaky one. THE LEAD REACHES 300!

An appeal for LBW has been turned down! Angles in a length delivery from outside off, Stokes walks across the stumps to flick it away but misses and wears it high on the pads. Colin appeals but nothing from the umpire. Height was an issue there.

FOUR! Poor start from de Grandhomme with the new ball. He has been trusted for the job and this isn't a good start. He comes from around the wicket and delivers it on the pads, too easy for Stokes as he works it down to fine leg for a boundary. To add to it, it's also called as a no ball as CdG overstepped.
Change of ends for Colin de Grandhomme.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Outside off, driven towards cover.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
On the pads, Jonny glances it down to long leg to get off the mark with a brace.
Fuller delivery on middle and leg, Stokes looks to flick but gets it off the inside edge down to fine leg for a single.
Boult comes running in and hurls it on a length around off, a little bit of shape away, Stokes is behind the line as he defends it down.
New Zealand going all out now. They have now taken the second new ball and Trent Boult returns to make first use of it. Two slips in place...

Huge shout for an LBW! Fuller in length around leg, Jonny looks to flick it away but misses to get rapped on the pads. Wagner cries his heart out but it's turned down. Hawk Eye shows why - pitching outside leg. What an over, Wagner has his tail up.
Fuller ball on off, pushed towards mid off.
Takes a stride forward and defends.
Fuller outside off, Bairstow leaves it alone.
Here comes the centurion of the first innings - Jonny Bairstow to replace his skipper.

OUT! Edged and Root doesn't get a ton, yet again! Some bad habits die hard. As they say, one brings two and that exactly is the case here. Let me tell you they haven't opted for the second new ball yet and it's the old cherry that has reaped them huge dividends as the two set batsmen depart in quick succession. Wagner too is among the wickets now, it's all happening out there. Are New Zealand back in it? Only time will tell. This is how the wicket fell - Fuller ball, sprayed wider outside off, the tactic which was used to dismiss Vince. Root, who was playing those deliveries so well this morning, edges one and Watling behind the stumps takes it easily. The long wait for a century from his bat continues. Last time it came in August 2017 against the Windies in Birmingham. Joe seriously needs to sort out this issue. His conversion rate is quite ordinary given his class and comparison among the Fab Four of the modern era.
Fuller outside off, left alone.
Ben Stokes is the new man in.

OUT! Stop the press! It's not the new ball bowler who has picked up a wicket for a change. Colin de Grandhomme has broken the deadlock in this Test match. Finally, some rejoice for New Zealand as they break the 97-run stand. A soft dismissal to term this and it's a wicket against the run of play. Fuller delivery, angling in on middle and leg, Dawid Malan walks across to flick it away but in the process, he loses his balance and ends up spooning a simple catch to Henry Nicholls at short mid-wicket. England's lead is 291!
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Good stop, Latham! Fuller delivery outside off, Dawid drives it crisply but Tom Latham at covers cuts it off with a dive to his right. Certainly saved a boundary.
Gets across to a length delivery and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
On middle and off, JR defends it down.
Good length delivery outside off, Joe Root cuts it nicely but Taylor at widish first slip dives full length to make a stop.
Stays back to a length delivery and with an open bat face he pushes it to the point region.
Fuller on the stumps, pushed to mid on.
Sprayed down the leg side again, Dawid missed his flick shot.

Huge appeal for LBW! Slower delivery from Wagner, pitches on middle, grips a touch on the surface and hits Malan on the pads who fails to put bat on ball. A loud appeal follows but the umpire shakes his head, gesturing that it is going down leg.
Good length ball on middle, kept out.
Bangs in a short ball but the line is on the leg stump, Malan moves inside the line to let it be.
Fuller and on the stumps, nudged towards mid on.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Clips one through backward square leg to cross ends.
Fullish delivery on off, driven towards the cover region.

FOUR! Streaky but Malan will take it, especially considering that he bagged a golden duck in the first innings. He has played a good hand here and now has a chance to score a ton. Fuller delivery outside off, Dawid goes hard at it. Gets a thick edge which flies safely through backward point for a boundary. The lead is now 289 and the partnership is 5 short of a century.
Leans across to a fuller ball and pushes it towards cover.
On a fuller length outside off, Root pats it towards cover. A maiden for Neil Wagner.

Good bowling! Root seemed to be frustrated after facing four dot balls and hence goes for an exciting shot. Wagner anticipates it as he hurls a slower one outside off, Root walks across the stumps and looks to whip it away but is done in by the lack of pace on it.
Pitched up delivery outside off, Root has driven it towards the cover fielder.
Short and outside off, steered off the back foot but straight to point.
Root drives it nicely towards mid off where Tom Latham fumbles but doesn't concede a run.
Fuller in length and outside off, driven on the up towards cover.
Good signs for the hosts as Tim Southee is back on the field.
In the channel outside off, Dawid lifts his bat to make a leave.
Malan wrists it towards mid on and shouts 'wait on!'.
On middle and leg, nudged with soft hands towards short mid-wicket.
Update - Tim Southee has a viral and hence is off the field. Maybe, that's the reason Kane Williamson has not adopted for the second new ball. Shows that he lacks trust in other bowlers.
Stays rooted inside the crease and cuts it square on the off side for a single.
Back of a length ball on middle and leg, tucked towards mid-wicket.
Harmless delivery outside off, it's left unharmed by Root.
Bends his back leg and eases this full ball towards deep point for a single.

Chance of a run out! My word, Malan would have been gone for all money. He clips this towards mid on and sets off. Matt Henry, the substitute fielder for Southee, charges to the ball and fires a flat throw at the bowler's end but misses his target as Dawid dives to get back in. Replays show the dive wouldn't have saved the southpaw had that hit the timber.
Fuller and on the pads, worked straight to mid on.
Fullish in length outside off, Dawid blocks it out well.
Length delivery, angling down leg, Malan looks to flick, he does so but not cleanly. The ball goes to the keeper who dives to his right and takes it on the bounce. They appeal but not given.
On a back of a length outside off, Malan keeps it out off the back foot.
Oh dear! Once again the ball slips out of Wagner's hand as he doles out a waist high full toss outside off, Root is happy to steer it through point for a single. Called a no ball.

Drinks called. It's been England's hour. They have come out with intent to score and have kept the run rate going at around 4 runs per over. The lead is 280 and both the batsmen are looking well set. Root has just notched up his fifty while Malan is inching closer to his. New Zealand bowlers are finding it really tough and there is the second new ball which they would be looking forward to, to get some success. Will the visitors continue to boss this session? Let's find out...
FOUR! Edged and through! Fuller ball, hurled wider outside off, Malan goes hard at it. Gets it off the edge which flies between backward point and gully for a streaky boundary.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.

Finally he gets to his half ton, 39th in Tests! The Barmy Army goes 'Rooooooooooooooot!' They just love doing this. Good length delivery on middle, Joe tucks it in front of square leg for a single. Raises his bat and acknowledges the cheer on offer. Has been a fluent knock so far. Can he double it?
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Angling in on middle and leg, worked towards the leg side.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Joe is happy to defend it down.
The second new ball is available now but not taken. Michael Atherton on air informs us that Tim Southee has left the field not sure why. Matt Henry is in as a substitute.
Another solid defense from Malan to end the 80th over.
Dropped on a back of a length outside off, Dawid hops back and crunches it through the gap at covers to add a couple more to his tally. England lead by 275 runs!
Around middle and leg, tucked into the leg side.
On a back of a delivery outside off, Dawid pushes it away off the back foot.
Fuller in length and outside off, a water-tight defense from the southpaw.
Fuller ball, angling in on middle, Malan is happy to nudge it away towards short mid-wicket.
Shortish on off, Root defends it back down on the pitch.
Good length delivery on the stumps, punched down the ground. Wagner is quick to put in a dive from mid on but couldn't prevent the single.
Angling in from around off, Malan presses ahead and blocks it out towards the cover fielder.
Malan is showing a lot of patience, gets a half-volley on off, he leaves it alone.
Another one on a fuller length, outside off, Dawid is happy to let it pass.
Fuller in length and outside off, shouldered arms to.
Gets across to a length delivery and nudges it towards mid on. Sodhi quickly moves across to his right and they decide not to run.
Tries to run it down to third man but it goes on the bounce to the gully fielder.
What was that? Maybe, Wagner attempted to bowl a yorker but this must have slipped out of his hands. A full toss, slower one on off, Root didn't pick it up as he mistimes his push towards cover.
Very full and hurled across Root who nicely gets to the pitch of the delivery and with his extended arms he drives it through cover-point for a brace. Moves to 49!
Pitched up on the stumps, nudged through backward square leg for a single.
Fuller in length and outside, Malan drives it towards wide mid off where Sodhi dives to his right to make a stop.
Shuffles a touch and helps a fuller ball on the pads down to fine leg for a single.
Presses forward to a fuller ball and blocks it out.
Beaten! Think it's the first time in the morning that this has happened! Fuller ball, tempting line, Malan looks to drive but fails to connect.
Fullish on the pads, worked away towards the man at short mid-wicket.
In the channel outside off, Malan leans across and shoulders his arms to it.
Fuller in length from around the wicket, Dawid offers a compact defense.
On the pads, glanced down to fine leg for a single.
Fullish in length and on the pads, clipped towards short mid-wicket.
On a back of a length outside off, Malan shows a straight bat in defense.

Chance of a run out and Root would have been in trouble! Fuller in length and outside off, Root eases it towards mid off and sets off. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses the stumps by just a bit. Tell you what, had that hit, Joe would have been struggling. Just noticed the stand started with 37 in the morning and in no time it has been reversed - 73 off just 141 balls.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short of a length delivery, angling away, steered towards backward point from within the crease.
Double change. Neil Wagner into the attack as well.
Treats Malan with a fuller ball first up, Malan leans forward to drive but mistimes it towards short cover. As mentioned in the insert, a tidy over from de Grandhomme to begin with.
Fuller but down leg, Root works it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Angling into the middle and leg stump, Joe Root wrists it once again to the same region.
Fullish on the pads, Root flicks it straight to the man at short mid-wicket.
Gets across to a fuller ball and pushes it towards mid on.
Fuller in length and angling in on middle, Root defends.
First change of the morning then. Colin de Grandhomme to bowl now. He's bowled a lot of overs in the series, has been pretty tidy but doesn't have that cutting edge, quips Atherton on air.

FOUR! And this time he does! He's not only a good driver of the cricket ball but also a puller. Doesn't back away from facing the short stuff. Swivels inside the crease and nails the pull behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
Bangs one short but the line is going down leg, Dawid looks to pull but fails to connect.
Short outside off, cut to deep backward point for a single.
Root is right behind the line and defends it solidly.
Taps this length delivery towards cover and gets one.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Malan defends.
Malan whips this delivery on the pads to mid-wicket and will retain strike.
Very full outside off, Root leans ahead and drives it square on the off side for a single.
Outside off, Root lifts his bat to make a leave.
Bangs one short on middle but without much venom, Malan swivels inside the crease as he pulls it through backward square leg for a single.

FOUR! Aahhh, shot! This is what got my colleague going. Yup, it was a treat to watch. A juicy half-volley outside off, Malan lunges forward and caresses it wide of the man at mid off for a boundary. No need to chase it. Brilliant!
On a length and outside off, defended off the back foot towards cover.
The idea was good but the execution wasn't. Shortish delivery outside off, Root makes room to dab it away past first slip but gets a bottom edge which goes on the bounce to Taylor.
Fullish again on middle and leg, wristed towards mid on.
Once again walks across, gets a full delivery on the stumps which he nudges through mid-wicket for a couple.

FOUR! This is good batting from Root! He shuffles across early and seeing this Southee fires full on the stumps. It goes a bit too straight which allows Joe to work it off his pads towards fine leg. No one manning that region and a boundary results.
Wide! That's a horrible delivery from Southee. Miles, miles outside off, it crosses the tramline and poor Watling has to move to his right to gather it.
Shortish delivery on off, Root punches it off the back foot towards cover.
Good length delivery, coming back in from outside off, Root looks to turn it away on the leg side but gets it off the leading edge. It's a soft one which rolls towards cover.
Back of a length delivery, angling in on middle and off, Dawid presents the full face of the bat.
Entices Malan to go after the pull shot as Boult bangs in a short one. The southpaw does feel for it at first but it's too high for him. He lets it sail over him to the keeper.
Hangs back to a length delivery and defends it out on the off side.
Once again a similar delivery, this time Root gets it past the man at cover-point for one.
Fuller and wider on off, searching for the edge is Boult but Root won't let him win. He presses ahead and strokes it towards cover-point.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Joe Root stays deep in the crease and looks to place his dab but finds the gully fielder.

50-run stand is up between the two! The duo is motoring along quite well and has looked unharmed. Gets a half-volley on off, Root unfurls a crisp drive towards sweeper cover for a single. The Barmy Army finds its voice again, actually they never lost it.
Looks to drive one through the line but mistimes it back to Southee who collects and mimes a throw back at the batsman.
Good length delivery on off, Root looks to dab it away but gets it off the outer part towards Williamson at backward point.
Sprayed on the pads, Malan walks across the stumps and works it fine down the leg side for an easy single.
Attacks the stumps again, Dawid stays back and keeps it out in front of the cover fielder.
Fuller and angling in on middle and off, Malan is compact in defense.
Wider on off, nothing doing, says Joe Root.
Back of a length delivery on middle, shown a straight bat.

FOUR! Square driven! Fuller delivery, served wider on off. Something that Trent Boult has been doing since yesterday. It fetched him the wicket of Vince but here Root plays well. Nicely bends his back knee, leans into it and drives it square through point for a boundary. Raval did give it a chase from backward point but to no avail.
Shortish on off, steered towards the point fielder for a quick single. England have come out with good positive intent to score this morning.
On a length and outside off, punched off the back foot towards point.

FOUR! Nicely done! Short of a length delivery outside off, with a bit of width on offer, Malan stands on top, rides the bounce and steers it behind point to pick the first boundary of the day. The stand moves into the 40s now.
A maiden for Southee. Root nicely makes a leave outside his off stump.
Sprays it wider outside off, Root has got nothing to do with that one.
Delivers it a bit wider on off, Root pushes it with soft hands towards cover.
In the corridor of uncertainty, JR plants his front foot across and makes a good-looking leave.
Stays right behind the line to this back of a length delivery and stabs it out towards cover.
On a length outside off, holding its line, Root shoulders his arms to it.
Tim Southee to have a go from the other end.
Slightly fuller in length on off, Dawid tries to defend again but this time he does so off the outer part of his willow as the ball rolls towards gully. A good first over from Trent.
On a length and outside off, Malan presses forward and defends it well.
Fuller delivery on off, Joe looks to drive but gets it off the inner edge through mid on for a single.

Good stop! Yes, New Zealand need this. They were really sloppy in the field last evening. Shortish delivery, close to the off stump line, Root arches back and cuts it nicely. Kane flies quickly to his right from gully and makes a one-handed stop. Remember, he took a blinder in the first Test? This was almost like that.
Drifts one on the pads, Malan glances it down to long leg to get to the other end. First run of the day for England.

An appeal to begin the day! But not given! Boult angles one into the southpaw from over the wicket, it skids a bit and pings Malan near the knee roll. He appeals but it is turned down almost instantly as it was easily heading down leg.

Huge cheer from the crowd as the players and umpires stride out to the middle. Joe Root and Dawid Malan are the overnight pair. Trent Boult to kickoff proceedings this morning. Two slips in place, here we go...

James Vince is up for a chat with David Lloyd. He is happy to have contributed with the bat. States they are in a good position now in this Test match and feels good about it. He's a bit gutted to have missed out on a ton yesterday. Opines the new ball does move around and it holds the key. Feels once it loses its shine the batting becomes easy. Credits the Kiwi bowlers for bowling really well throughout the game and admits that they did put them under pressure.

Pitch report - Scott Styris says the pitch is still a good one with absolutely no demons in it. Adds the footmarks are there but wouldn't be that threatening for the spinners to come to the party. Feels it's not going to be a tough task for the Kiwis to play out time as batting last on it shouldn't be too concerning. Simon Doull adds picking wickets wouldn't be easy on this surface and hence setting funky fields could fetch you some.

New Zealand did start well on Day 3 by reducing the deficit but their bowlers couldn't create much of an impact later in the day. The pitch seemed to have flattened out and it was very much evident with the way the Kiwi pacers bowled. There is a bit of turn on offer but it's not that alarming. The hosts would need to come out with a plan and try to pick up quick wickets if they are to stand a chance. What's in store for today? Runs or wickets? We shall find out in just a bit...

The first three days started with the Test hanging right in the balance but today it's England who are right on top. Stoneman and Vince's knocks have put them in the ascendancy and they now have Root in the middle who looks set for a big one. The lead already reads 231 runs and the question arises is how much they will feel is enough before putting the Kiwis in to bat.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Root and Malan then got together and made sure there is no further hiccup. They have strung another unbeaten 37-run stand which has only tired out the bowlers. New Zealand were a bit sloppy in the field as they dropped a few catches and missed a couple of run out chances as well. Once again a regular sight was seen - Boult and Southee amongst the wickets as rest couldn't do anything. Right then, England are in a commanding position and with two full days to go, it will be interesting to see if they bat on or plan to declare. Should be another fascinating day of cricket. Do join us on Monday to see how the penultimate day pans out. Cheers!

The two down-on-confidence men - Stoneman and Vince stepped up and delivered when it required the most. They dealt with everything thrown at them and grew in confidence to not let the hosts run away with the show. Together they were involved in a stoic 123-run stand and were motoring along nicely till the Tea break. Come the final session, they had the opportunity to score their respective tons but failed to do so. Both departed rather quickly after scoring their fifties but not before laying the platform for others to build on.

An attritional day of Test cricket comes to an end. England have come out on top here as they have swelled the lead to 231 runs. The day started with the Kiwi tail (Southee, Wagner and Boult) wagging and frustrating the Englishmen to an extent. It meant that, the visitors could only get a lead of 29 runs heading into third innings. The Kiwis had the momentum going into the break and they drew advantage home when they nipped out Cook immediately after Lunch.

It has gone really dark and it doesn't please the umpires. They come together, take the reading and ask the players to leave the field. So, twice in two days, the bad light has cost us a few overs. STUMPS ON DAY 3!
Gets a long away across to a fuller ball outside off and mistimes his drive towards mid off.
Sees the ball pass past his off stump.
Very full on the off stump, Root jams it out towards cover.
Fuller in the zone on off, blocked solidly off the front foot.
Fuller ball down leg, clipped towards fine leg. They look for the second but it isn't on.
Length ball outside off, defended off the back foot.

FOUR! Picks up the length early and bashes it, Root! Sodhi drops it short and was asking to be hit. Joe doesn't disappoint him as he rocks back quickly to pull it over mid-wicket. The stand moves to 36 while the 200 for England is also raised with this boundary.
Turning in from a shorter length outside off, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.
Flicked through the leg side for one more.
Punched past the cover fielder for a single.

No bat involved! And the Kiwis have now lost both their reviews! A loopy leg break, pitching on the rough and turning in towards leg. Malan walks across the stumps to flick it away but seems to have missed it. There is some noise though as the ball passes the bat and Watling behind the stumps takes it sharply to his right. He puts in a strong appeal but the umpire shakes his head. The hosts get together and opt for the UDRS. Nothing is seen on the Snicko and Hot Spot. They now check for the LBW. Hawk Eye shows it's in line but would have gone on to miss the leg stump.
Huge, huge shout for a catch down the leg side. It's Watling who looks really excited. The Kiwis think for a while before taking the DRS...
Flighted delivery outside off, pushed through cover for a single.
Presses forward and pushes it to covers. Loud and clear calling from Joe as they collect a single.
Too full and on off, driven straight to mid off.
Root has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A shorter length ball outside off, Root defends it down.

Big mix-up, nearly a run out! Too full in length and outside off, Root reaches out for it and drives it towards covers. He sets off for a run but after seeing the fielder getting to the ball quickly, he stops and sends his partner back. Malan is almost mid-way down the track as he turns back to rush in. Henry Nicholls in the meantime collects the ball and throws it towards the bowler's end. Misses the target. Maybe, Nicholls was a shade late in releasing the ball.
Neil Wagner would try to create a breakthrough here.
Good length delivery on off, Root stays on the back foot and defends it to the off side.
Takes a stride ahead to a loop leg break and hits it through point for a single.
Turning away from off, Root plants his front foot across, covers the turn and lets it pass.
Quicker delivery, a bit too full, Root prods ahead in defense.
Lets the ball turn in from outside off, walks across and tucks it past short leg for one more.
Loops it up outside off, it's driven square on the off side for a single.
Quicker ball, fired outside off, left alone.
Shortish ball on off, too close to cut but Root still attempts it. Chops it through gully and shall retain strike after taking a run.
Edgeeeeed but it doesn't carry! Delivers it on a length and moves away a bit, Root tries to run it down but the ball goes off the edge but drops in front of the man at widish first slip.
Short of a length ball outside off, blocked off the back foot.
And there you go. Almost! Fuller and getting the ball to reverse but it's too straight. Malan clips it off the pads behind square on the leg side and gets to the other end.
Drops it on a back of a length on middle, stabbed towards cover. Boult is making Malan stay deep in the crease. Watch out for that yorker, Dawid.
Skiddy delivery on a good length, Malan stays back and keeps it out gently.
Flatter ball outside off, punched off the back foot towards cover-point.
Gives it a nice loop, it dips it on middle, Joe gets down on one knee and slogs it wide of Wagner at mid on. The big pacer gives it a chase to keep them down to two.
Malan gets back to a leg break and punches it in front of the cover fielder for a quick single.
Turning in from outside off, Dawid walks across and clips it towards square leg.
Floated delivery, landed full outside off, Root presses forward and with an open face of the bat he pushes it through point for a single.
Starts this spell with a loopy leg break but it's on the shorter side outside off, Malan slaps it square on the off side for a single.
Ish Sodhi will replace Neil Wagner now.
Another one angling away on off, Root has got nothing to do with that one.
Boult is switching angles too often. Now back to over the wicket and hurls across Root. Left unharmed.
Shoulders his arms to a ball on a fuller length outside off.
Comes from around the wicket and delivers in on middle and leg, Root clips it through mid-wicket. Wants two and gets it comfortably in the end.
Another one on a similar length, no shot offered.
Sprays it too wide outside off, almost crosses the tramline, nothing doing says Root.
Coming back in from outside off, Malan points his bat upwards to make a leave.
Shorter ball with width on offer, steered through backward point for two runs.
Fuller in length on off, Malan reaches out for it as he extends his arms and drives it to mid off for nothing.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Nicely done! Malan gets on top of the bounce and cuts it with finesse through backward point for a boundary.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Malan crunched it past cover for a brace.
Back of a length delivery on off, a water-tight defense from the English run-machine. Maiden for TB.
Once again changes the angle, bowls a slower fuller delivery outside off, Joe drives it to the cover fielder.
Now from around the wicket, Boult angles in on middle, it's tucked away off the back foot by Root to mid-wicket.
Too wide outside off, Root shows interest in going after it but then holds back and lets it pass.
Root in his typical style arches back to a short of a length delivery and punches it square towards gully at Williamson.
Slants it again from a back of a length outside off, the angle takes it further away as the English skipper doesn't play at it.
Pitched up delivery on off, Malan lunges forward and offers the straightest of bats.
Harmless delivery outside off, shouldered arms to.
Hangs back to a length delivery and knocks it back to Wagner.
This one nips back in a touch from outside off but Dawid Malan trusts the bounce and makes a leave. It just goes over the off pole. Close!
Tempting line, in the channel of hesitation, Dawid Malan doesn't offer any stroke.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, nudged towards the fielder at short mid-wicket.
Switches the angle for the last ball of the over, comes around the wicket and digs in a short ball outside off, Root keeps it out with an angled bat to gully.
Trent slants it really full, a half-volley wider outside off, Joe bends his back leg, leans into it and drives it neatly but can't pierce the gap through cover.
Ahead of a length, angling away outside off, Root gets back and with a straight bat punches it to the cover fielder.
Lets the ball come to him and then opens the face of the bat to dab it in the same region.
Shorter in length on off, Root cuts it late towards the gully fielder.
Boult once again hurls it across the batsman, Joe Root is happy to leave it unharmed.
Hangs back to a short of a length ball outside off and defends it towards cover.
Keeps it nice and full on middle and off, DM bunts it off the front foot to mid off.
On a length and holding its line, Malan lifts his bat to make a leave.
Back of a length delivery outside off, punched off the back foot towards cover.
Fuller in length and a touch wide outside off, Malan shoulders his arms to it.
Fuller and down leg, helped off the pads by Root to fine leg for an easy single.
Low full toss right at the base of the stumps, kept out by Malan.
Fuller and speared in on middle, worked towards mid on for nothing.
FOUR! Dawid Malan is off the pair! Boult bangs in a short one, Malan stays back and hits it across the line. It goes aerial and past the diving square leg fielder for a boundary.
Fuller and searching for the LBW, Malan is quick to whip it away towards mid-wicket.
Arches back to a short ball and places the cut shot wide of the gully fielder for one.
Fuller ball on off, driven square but straight to the point fielder.
Hangs back to a back of a length delivery and shows a straight bat.
Shorter delivery, once again on off, Malan makes a watchful leave again.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Another one in the similar channel, Malan is happy to make another leave.
Good length delivery, closer to off stump, left alone.
Back of a length on middle and leg, tucked through backward square leg for a single.
Dawid Malan is in next.

OUT! James Vince edges one and misses out on a well-deserved ton! Boult was trying this ploy for quite some time and persisted with it. Delivers a fuller length ball, it's sprayed wider outside off, Vince runs out of patience as he goes hard fishing at it. Ekes out a thick outside edge towards first slip where Ross Taylor takes a smart catch to his left with both the hands. He shelled one earlier when he went with just one hand but not this time. England are effectively 194/3.
Very full outside off, Root crouches low and squeezes it past the man at point for a single.
Pitches it up again, this time a bit closer on off, Vince drills it square on the off side for a single.
Sprays it very full and slants it really wide outside off, James Vince keeps his calm and lets it pass.
On a back of a length outside off, a strong back foot punch offered but finds the cover fielder.
A touch fuller outside off, driven crisply through cover for a single.

Drinks break. England continue to be on top. They are going strongly in spite of losing Mark Stoneman in the session. Both Vince and Root have looked at ease so far. New Zealand dropped a couple of catches after Tea but luckily for them it didn't cost them much. 18 overs left in the day's play, let's see if the Kiwis make a comeback...
Shortish around leg, Root tucks it through mid-wicket for a single. 7 from this over, the lead is now 191 runs!
Reaches out for a length ball outside off, strokes it to deep point for one.
Short and on middle, pulled through square leg for a single.
FOUR! Wagner once again pitches it short, around middle and leg, Root loves it there. He swivels and pulls it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. No run.
Wagner is back in the attack and digs in a short ball outside off, Root lets it through to the keeper.
Shortish and around leg, pulled down to fine leg where the fielder made a fine stop. Two runs added to the total.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region. One run added to the total.

Beaten! Root watches the width outside off and spots the chance to free his arms. Flashes his blade at it but misses. He is been watched by his parents, who are in attendance today, informs Michael Atherton on air.
Serves it full and outside off, it's driven down the ground but straight to mid off.
Angling away from the batsman, a bit on the shorter side, Root tries to run it down to third man but fails to middle it properly.
Starts with a length ball around leg and middle, Root gets behind the line and defends it back.
Trent Boult is brought back into the attack.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Straighter in line, Vince quietly flicks it through square leg and returns for the second run.
Brings a full ball back into the batsman, around middle and leg, Vince flicks it on the leg side and one of the two mid-wicket fielders stops it.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Plays a full length ball with gentle hands to mid on and pinches a quick single. The fielder has a shy but fails to find the target. That throw nearly hit Root.
Angles in a length ball on off, Root presents a straight bat in defense.
Full and outside off, driven away from his body but straight to covers.
Shuffles across the stumps and helps it wide of mid on for a single.
Covers the line of attack and blocks it to the off side.
Takes his front leg forward and defends it watchfully.
Fuller and on off, driven back to the bowler.
Good length delivery outside off, Root goes on the back foot but fails to middle his attempted punch shot.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks it. End of a successful over!
Back of a length ball on middle, worked on the leg side.
Vince has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fullish and around middle and leg, it's eased down to fine leg for a run.
Joe Root arrives next.

OUT! Finally a catch has been taken and Stoneman has run out of his luck. Once again he goes chasing after a wide delivery outside off and nicks it behind. Watling dives to his left to complete a wonderful catch. Dropped on 48 and 57, Mark fails to make it big. End of a 123-run stand and England lead by 176 runs. A stat - This is the 50th time that Southee and Watling have been involved together in a dismissal, highest for the Black Caps. Great combo!
Back of a length delivery on off, Stoneman goes on the back foot and defends it on the leg side.
Angling into the batsman from outside off, Vince gets forward to defend but it takes the inside edge and strikes him on the pads.
On a length around off, Vince plays it late and taps it down to point.
Angles in a length ball on off, James presents a straight bat in defense.
Vince as defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Bouncer around leg, well over the batsman's head, Vince allows it through. Called a wide.
Gentle movement back into the left-hander from outside off, Stoneman stays back and plays it through point for a run.
In the channel outside off, it's left alone.
Around off, watchfully played to the off side to end the over. That was a slower one bowled at 106.7. The batsmen did well there to read it.
Strides forward to a full ball and drives it to mid off.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Better this time. Stays back and cuts it through point for a run. Key part was that he was not looking to go hard at it.
Stoneman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Play and a miss! Width on offer outside off, shorter in length, Stoneman swishes and misses. He has become a bit loose after getting to his fifty and needs to get his composure back.
Once again Vince is forward as he pushes it to mid on again.
Full and angling in on middle, pushed down to mid on.
Width on offer outside off, it's steered through point for a couple.
Rocks on the back foot and punches it straight to point.
Gets forward to a full ball and blocks.

DROPPED! Another chance goes down begging at wide first slip. Tim Southee is the culprit this time. A touch short in length outside off, Stoneman tries to punch it through the line but gets an outside edge behind. Southee stretches to his left but it deflects off his hands and goes to third man. A single taken.
Another good looking drive by Vince but he finds the cover fielder.
Fullish and on middle, driven firmly but straight to mid on.
Played to the point region by the batsman. No run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fuller in length outside off, driven confidently down to mid off.
Lands it on a length just outside off, Vince remains back footed as he defends it back.
Keeps it full and on middle, it's flicked off the inner half of the bat to square leg for one.
Good length ball around off, it's hit on the up, remains aerial for a while but goes safely to covers.
Fuller and straighter, pushed straight to mid on again.
Angling into the batsman, Vince pushes it down to mid on.
It's been driven superbly through the covers. They pick up a single. This now is the highest score in Tests for Mark Stoneman.
Pitches it full and around off, Vince drives wide of the cover fielder for a single.
Wayward delivery. Attempts the slower one but it's direction-less. Way down the leg side and Stoneman has nothing to do with it.
Southee bowls it full and outside off, Vince drives it square of the wicket on the off side for one. Doing it with ease.
Full and outside off, driven through cover-point for a brace.
FOUR! Southee gets the reverse swing going, but serves it too full in length, around off and it's driven down the ground past the diving mid on fielder for a boundary. Well played.
Play and a miss! A speedy delivery, landing on a good length outside off, Vince tries to cut from the crease but it beats his bat. Extra bounce there.
Good length ball outside off, angling away at a gentle pace, Stoneman stays back and plays it through cover-point for a run.
Short and wide outside off, Mark camps back and slaps it over point for a single.
Stoneman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Lets out a full delivery outside off, Stoneman plays a confident front foot drive but finds mid off.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball and drives it straight towards the cover fielder.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

A touch short and around off, Vince hangs on the back leg and hammers it across the line. It races through and so does the square leg fielder. He puts in a good effort to reach to the ball and stop it from crossing the rope. Saves a run for his side.
Angling down the leg side, on a length, it's worked off the pads to long leg for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, it's played down from the crease towards cover-point.
A little bit of inward movement there as it lands on a fuller length around middle, Vince flicks it from the inner half to mid-wicket.
Gets back and uses the width to punch it through the cover region. A single taken.
Full and outside off, Stoneman this time lets it be.

FOUR! Edgy. A streaky way to reach his half century, 5th in Tests. Southee is on the shorter side outside off, Stoneman flashes his blade through the line and edges it over the slip cordon for a boundary. He raises his bat towards the dressing room. A vital knock for his career and also for England. The lead has crossed the 150-run mark.
Serves it full and outside off, it's stroked off the front foot to extra cover.
A mistimed drive by Vince towards mid off.
Once again attempts to force the issue on the off side but gets an inside edge through his legs to square leg. A single taken.
Reaches out for a full ball outside off and drives it through the line. Finds the cover fielder.
Shortish and outside off, punched to short cover.
Gets on the front foot to a full ball and drives it to mid off.
A little short in length around off, Vince goes on his toes in defense.
Short outside off, cut straight to the point fielder.
Shortish and on off, defended down to towards mid on.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

NOT OUT! New Zealand lose their review. A delivery sliding down the leg side, Vince attempts to flick but fails to connect. There is some sound as it goes behind to the keeper. Watling collects the ball and they appeal vociferously. Nothing from the umpire and Southee along with Watling convinces his skipper to take the DRS. The replays roll in but fails to find any wood. It has clipped the trousers and that's why there was some noise.
Appeal for a caught behind down the leg side. Not given but Southee and Watling are convinced. They suggest Kane Williamson to take the DRS. Let's see.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tim Southee to operate from the other end.
Watchfully leaves a length ball outside off to end an eventful over.

DROPPED BY TAYLOR! Should have gone with both hands, Rosco. A shortish ball just outside off, too close to cut but Stoneman still attempts it. He gets a thick outside edge while doing so and it flies behind. Taylor at wide first slip sticks his right hand out but fails to hold on to the catch. Stoneman survives.
Watches the width outside off and goes after it. Ends up flashing and missing.

EDGY FOUR! Excellent delivery by Colin. He angles in a length ball around middle, getting it to nip away a shade, Stoneman tries to defend it with a vertical bat but it takes the outside edge and speeds through the gap between keeper and wide first slip for a boundary.
Width on offer outside off, it's guided down to third man and they take the second run. The fielder returns the throw to the keeper but Stoneman is safely in before that.
Starts with a gentle good length delivery in the channel outside off, Stoneman allows it through to the keeper.

Out walk the concerned players along with the umpires. The Kiwi huddle disperses as the fielders take their respective positions. Mark Stoneman will be on strike and he will face Colin de Grandhomme. A widish slip in place for him...
... Day 3, Final session ...

The current stand is worth 89 runs with the lead just 8 short of 150. Vince has gone past the fifty-run mark while his partner is just 8 away from his. The pitch looks good to bat on and these two have certainly made merry on it. Can the New Zealand bowlers break this stand or will the current pair continue to flourish? Join us in a short while to find out...

England's session. They lost Alastair Cook quickly after Lunch as Boult for the 4th time in a row got the better of him in this series. Now the onus was on the two men - Stoneman and Vince as to what they would do to cement their place in the side. They needed to play an innings of substance and are surely on course for it. The latter came out with positive intent and was eager to keep the scoreboard ticking along. Stoneman though looked uncertain at the start but as the time has passed, he seems to be finding his groove.
Flattish ball outside off, Vince gets across and then makes a leave. TEA, DAY 3.
Short and turning in from outside off, Stoneman delays his cut shot as he hits it pretty late behind point to get to the other end.
Slower through the air, landing full around off, pushed towards mid off.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Pushes a loopy ball through covers for a single.
Quicker one delivered outside off, nothing doing.
Last over before Tea...
Bangs in a short one, Stoneman at first looks to take on the pull shot but then at the last moment he decides to duck.
Stays behind the line and stabs it out.
Back of a length delivery, climbing off the deck, Mark hops back and defends it down.
Shortish again but around leg, Vince helps it down to long leg for one. 111/1 England!
Shortish on the hips, tucked down to fine leg for a single.
Short and angling down leg, easily ducked under.

FOUR! That's fifty for James Vince, his third in this format. Vince needed this to con-vince the selectors that what he is capable of. Has looked really solid since the start of this innings and his score is there to defend him. Generously tossed up ball outside off, James leans into it and drives it along the carpet through covers to reach a much-needed milestone. His stand with Stoneman is 85 with the lead reading 138. Also, his knock is studded with nine boundaries so far.
Wrong one around middle, Vince hangs back in defense.
FOUR! Too easy for James Vince! Sodhi drops it short on middle and leg, the right-hander is quick to camp back and pull it with disdain through square leg for a boundary. Moves to 49.
Bowls a googly, turning in, Vince deals off the back foot.
Nicely bowled! Loops it up on the rough outside off, Vince prods forward to defend but the ball spins away to beat the outside edge of his bat.
Stays back to a loopy leg break and works it with the turn through square leg for a single.
Works it off the pads towards fine leg and gets to the other end does Stoneman. England's 100 is up for the loss of Alastair Cook, says Atherton on air.
Digs in a short one but the line is outside off, MS is happy to let it pass.
Shortish on middle and leg, tucked past short leg and they will get a brace.
Stoneman picks up the short ball early and ducks under it.
Shovels a bit and fetches it to deep square leg for a single.
FOUR! All along the ground! Short ball on the leg stump, Vince plays a controlled pull shot along the ground through fine leg and picks up a boundary.
Serves a leg spinner outside off, turning back in, Stoneman gets his front leg forward and then lets it be. Not too far from the off pole.
Googly on middle, flicked in front of square leg for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Gets forward and pushes at it. It probably spins away a bit and rolls towards backward point for a single.
Slower through the air, nicely tossed up and full around off, Stoneman pushes it to covers.
Floated leg spinner on off, driven square of the wicket on the off side for a quick single.

Off the shoulder, indeed! Good review from Stoneman. The on-field decision has to be overturned. To be honest, even we felt that it has taken the edge. Wagner comes from over the wicket, hits the deck hard and angles it in around off. Mark Stoneman tries fending it by hopping in the crease but the ball seems to have taken the outer edge. Watling tumbles to his left to take it and they all go up in a celebratory appeal. In fact, Wagner is off for a run already as he is all pumped up. The umpire raises the finger as well. Stoneman can't believe it and signals to his partner that it has gone off his shoulder before taking the DRS. Snicko appears and it doesn't show any spike, there is nothing spotted on the Hot Spot either. So, clearly no bat involved and Mark Stoneman isn't going anywhere. It was off his shoulders only. New Zealand's celebrations have been cut short. Our colleague following the match from home first found it amazing that Stoneman has reviewed it. But then after watching the replays, he considered it a terrific use of the technology. Sums it up by saying, on the first impression, Mark was stoned but on the final impression, we are stoned. Please notice the wordplay there.
A caught behind appeal is upheld by the umpire. Wagner is already celebrating. But Stoneman feels he hasn't edged this and gestures towards his shoulders. Takes the review straightaway...
Shortish delivery down leg, Stoneman leaves it alone.
Gets on top of the bounce and pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
Short and down leg, helped towards fine leg for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Comes from around the wicket, bangs in a short one, it's tapped on the bounce to short leg.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up on off, James looks to drive it away but the ball spins past the outside edge of his bat and Bairstow behind the stumps fails to collect it cleanly.
Floated delivery around middle and off, Vince blocks it out.
Flattish on middle, defended off the back foot.
Tossed up on off, patted through cover for a single.
Works it off the inner half past short leg.
Good length delivery outside off, MS stays back to block but gets it off the edge down to third man for a single.
Another bounce, two in a row and same result, Mark ducks.
Bangs in a short one on middle, Stoneman ducks under it.
On a length and closer to the off stump line, Mark Stoneman defends it off the back foot.
Goes fuller and angles it in on middle, it's driven on the up to mid on.
Back of a length delivery on middle and off, Stoneman shows a straight bat in defense.
Goes back to this short ball and pushes it towards the point fielder.
Flatter through the air, blocked into the ground.
Around middle and leg, worked away through square leg for a single.
The length is dragged short, it's around off and Vince pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Spinning back into the batsman from around off, Stoneman leans to defend but it takes the inside edge, brushes his pads and rolls past short leg for a single.
Floated full on off, it's driven down to mid off for a quick single.
Shortish and on off, defended off the back foot to end the over.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Stoneman plays it off his back foot to point.
Keeps it full and on off, it's driven to covers.
Angling back into the batsman from a length outside off, Stoneman blocks it from the back foot.
Lands it on a length and outside off, Stoneman punches it down from the crease to covers.
Vince has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Looking in imperious form. Sodhi flights it up and drops it too full and wide outside off, Vince strides forward and drives it beautifully through covers.
Comes from round the wicket for the left-hander and bowls it around off, it's punched through covers for a run.
Catch it is the shout but it doesn't carry. Sodhi drags his length short to which Vince pulls. He fails to keep it down though. It goes on one bounce to Latham at deep square leg. A single taken.
A touch quicker and flatter on off, Vince goes on the back foot and defends it with the spin.
Floated leg spinner on off, it's defended back from the inner part of the bat.
Short ball on off, pulled across the line to deep square leg for a run.
Slants across the stumps, on a length, it's driven on the up but straight to the cover fielder.
Full and around off, James gets across the stumps and blocks it back.
Beaten! This one leaves the batsman after landing around off, Vince pushes at it and misses.
Identical to the last delivery, once again Vince comes up with a back foot defense.
Angling away from the batsman, on a length, Vince defends it from the crease.
Plays it with the spin but straight to mid-wicket.
Turning into the batsman from around off, Stoneman blocks.
A touch short and punched through covers for a run. 50-run stand comes up between the two. They have stabilized the innings so far.
Another wrong 'un, on the shorter side, Vince defends it by going on the back foot.
Probably a googly, landing full around off, Vince lunges and defends it from the inner half of the bat.
Tossed up ball around leg, too full in length, Stoneman flicks it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
A front foot defense to complete the over.
Oversteps and concedes a no ball. Another drive from the bat of Stoneman but he finds the mid off fielder. Lead is now 100!
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
An inviting length outside off, Stoneman drives but fails to get the timing right. Finds mid off.
Bowls it wide outside off, it's allowed through to the keeper.
Full and shaping back into the batsman from outside off, Stoneman defends solidly.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On the pads, flicked behind square leg for a couple.
Just short of leg gully. A low full toss around off, Vince paddle sweeps it a bit uppishly but doesn't carry to the fielder.
Loopy and drifting around off, Vince prods forward in defense.
Gets on the front foot again as he defends it back.
Flighted full on off, defended back off the front foot.
A leg gully in place for James Vince.
A nicely tossed up leg spinner, landing full outside off, Stoneman presses forward to defend but it takes the inside edge and goes past short leg for a run.
Ish Sodhi gets the chance to roll his arm now. A slip and short leg in place.

Drinks break. Alastair Cook got dismissed in the last hour but the current pair has not bogged down. James Vince, in particular, has looked convincing and together with Mark Stoneman, he has kept the Kiwi bowlers at bay. The lead is 96 now.
FOUR! Glorious. De Grandhomme delivers it a little too full around off and Vince drives it with elegance through mid on for a boundary.
Angles it into the batsman, Vince fails to flick it off his pads.
Beaten! This one holds its line after landing on a length outside off, Vince pushes at it flat-footed and gets beaten.
Another loose drive attempted by Vince and he gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Not quite where he intended. Tries to push a length ball through covers but gets an inside edge. It rolls through square leg and they take a brace.
Drops it on a fuller length outside off, Vince drives off the front foot, once again excellent timing but he finds the mid off fielder.
Bouncer, the batsman ducks. The first of many to come, feels Michael Atherton on air.
Good length ball just outside off, it's punched from the back foot to covers.
Pitches it up and Stoneman is forward in defense.
Remains inside the crease and defends it on the leg side.
Fetches a short delivery from outside off and pulls it in front of square leg for a run.
Around off, on a length, angling away, Vince gets forward and pushes it towards cover-point.
On a length outside off, it's left alone.
Goes on the back foot to punch it through the line but it takes a bit of an outside edge and drops in front of second slip.
Stoneman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
FOUR! Nicely played! A touch short in length around off, Stoneman rocks back, gets closer to the line of the delivery and steers it wide of backward point for a boundary.
Too full and on off, it's driven off the front foot, good connection but it goes straight to mid off.
A tempter outside off, on a driving length, Stoneman strides forward and then shoulders arms.
Beauty, nipping away from a length around off, Vince without any footwork pushes inside the line and misses.
Shortish and outside off, moving away a bit, Vince leaves it.
FOUR! Vince is oozing confidence. Wagner angles across a full ball outside off, James loves it there. He takes a stride forward and drives it crisply through covers for a glorious boundary.
Vince has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Full in length wide outside off, Vince shoulders arms.
Neil Wagner is unleashed into the attack.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.
Plays a delivery outside off to point. Needs to be careful here, especially when the bowler is bowling from round the wicket angle.
In the channel outside off, Stoneman allows it through.
A touch short and moving away, Stoneman pushes inside the line and misses.
FOUR! Shot of the innings, so far! Colin overpitches it outside off, Stoneman strides forward and unfurls a gorgeous cover drive for a boundary.
Outside off, left alone.
Boult runs in from round the wicket and angles in a length ball on off, Vince doesn't get any room to work with and defends it back.
Plays it with an open face! A little bit of width outside off, James quietly dabs it past the slip region for a couple of runs.
Drives a full ball through the line but once again fails to pick the gap.
Keeps it full and around off, it's driven off the front foot but straight to the extra cover fielder.
Another delivery which is angled away from the right-hander, too wide outside off and James makes a leave.
Angling away from the batsman, on a length, Vince defends it from the crease to the off side.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
A delivery on the pads, it's helped behind square leg for one.
Remains back footed and offers a straight bat in defense.
Vince has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Huge shout for an lbw, the umpire remains unmoved. Too full in length and angling into the batsman, lands around middle and leg, Vince fails to flick and is hit on the pads. They put in an unsuccessful appeal. Kane Williamson looks interested in taking the DRS but Colin doesn't want it. The replays show that it's comfortably missing leg.
Starts with a fuller length ball on middle, it's flicked on the leg side but straight to mid-wicket.
Colin de Grandhomme to bowl. He has a couple of slips in place.
Angling in on off, fuller in length, Stoneman strides ahead and defends it back.
Slants it around middle and leg, Stoneman works it towards square leg.
Full and angling into the batsman, Mark plays an on drive but finds the fielder.
Drops it on a length around off, Stoneman tries to push at it but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
FOUR! Stoneman has played a cracking back foot punch for a boundary. He judged the line and length very early, nicely gets on top of the bounce and executes his shot with perfection.
Boult hurls this one on the pads and Stoneman eases it fine down the leg side for a brace.

FOUR! Dealing in boundaries at the moment, Vince trying to convince everyone here! Once again shows no mercy to a delivery which is on the shorter side outside off. Packs a punch and it speeds through point.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Digs in a short ball and it's pulled across the line by Stoneman. Not properly timed but it lobs down safely towards fine leg for a run.
Bowls it in the line of the stumps, Stoneman covers the line and blocks it safely.
A free flowing drive this time from the bat of Mark but he fails to find the gap.
A stifled appeal for an lbw as Stoneman fails to flick a leg stump line delivery. The umpire shows no interest and the replays detect an inside edge. Good decision.
A back foot defense on the on side to end the over.
FOUR! Boult offers width outside off, Vince's eyes lit up as he latches onto the room and smacks it square of the wicket on the off side for a boundary.
Serves it on a length around off, Vince gets behind the line in defense.
Plays it down in the gap on the off side and rotates the strike.
Shortish and on off, Stoneman blocks it from the back foot.
Slants in a length ball on middle and off, it's defended towards mid-wicket.
Goes on his back foot and pushes it on the off side for a run.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Southee once again takes this one away with the angle, Stoneman pokes inside the line and gets a little outside edge. It rolls towards the slip cordon.
On a length and outside off, Mark shoulders arms.
Reaches out for a delivery outside off and plays it down to point.
Angling away from the batsman, on a good length, Stoneman allows it through.
FOUR! Crunching shot! Not too full as it lands outside off. Vince is forward in no time and smashes it through covers to get off the mark with a boundary.
Vince has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
James Vince walks in next at number 3.

OUT! Boult strikes to remove Cook again! Four times in four innings, he is clearly having an edge over the England great. Serves it on a length outside off, Cook stays back and has a needless push inside the line. Gets a fat outside edge behind and BJ Watling makes no mistake. Could have easily left this one. In the Auckland Test, he edged one in the slip cordon but that time the line of the delivery was around middle and off. Clearly, Cook is struggling here. This is the ninth time overall that Trent has dismissed him in Test cricket. Bunny! Ian Smith on air with a big question - Was this the last Test innings of Alastair Cook? Hmm...overseas perhaps, at home not sure.
Helps it off his pads to backward square leg and rotates the strike.
Play and a miss! Width on offer outside, short in length as well, Stoneman tries to flat bat it but misses.
Drifting down the leg side, Stoneman fails to work it off his pads.

FOUR! Poor delivery and punished. Short and wide outside off, Cook rocks back and slaps it through the point region for a cracking boundary. Should be looking to pitch it up and get it to move from this 'round the wicket angle.
A good looking drive by Cook, but he finds the cover fielder. He's moving well.
Changes his angle and steams in from around the wicket. Serves it full and outside off, Cook defends it from the crease.
Strides forward to a full ball and strokes it down to mid off.
Beaten! This one is angled away from the batsman, Cook feels for it as he pushes at it tamely but misses.
FOUR! Shot! Cook is looking good so far. Very positive. Receives a short delivery in his half and puts it away in style. Rides the bounce and pulls it with good timing to the deep mid-wicket fence.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Angling into the batsman on a good length, Stoneman defends it on the leg side.

Direct hit was needed there! Once again Stoneman works it off his pads towards mid-wicket and eyes a single. Although, seeing the mid on fielder charging to it, he sends his partner back. The fielder misses his shy otherwise it would have been a close case.
Boult keeps his line straight, Mark turns it around off his pads to mid-wicket.
Serves one down the leg side, Stoneman tries to flick but misses. We have seen a few wickets going down to this type of delivery in this series.
Bangs it in short on middle and leg, Cook pulls it down towards long leg and takes a run.
FOUR! That's well played! Southee serves it around off, a touch on the shorter side, Stoneman punches it sweetly off his back foot to the cover boundary.
Hurls it wide outside off, Stoneman has nothing to do with it.
Around off on a length, Mark defends it off his back foot.

A bit edgy! Southee bowls it on a good length around off, Stoneman stays back to play inside the line. Tries to open the face but it takes the edge and races through the gap between gully and point. A couple of runs taken.
Slips another delivery down the leg side, it's left alone by Stoneman.
Starts with a length ball angling down the leg side, Cook picks it off his pads and helps it through backward square leg. The fine leg fielder quickly gets around and they take a single.
